summary.text: 東, “east,” began as a picture of a bag tied at both ends. The drawing was borrowed for its sound to write the direction. Its later resemblance to a sun inside a tree has produced an appealing sunrise story, but that does not explain the early shape.

formation.text: An object pictograph was borrowed for the word “east.”

components.text: The whole outline represents a tied bag in this account. Apparent 日 and 木 shapes are not separate original sun and tree components.

history.text: The direction use is already present in oracle-bone and bronze writing. Thus the character’s later everyday meaning belongs to its borrowed use, while the shape preserves the older object picture.

uncertainties.text: Descriptions of the object vary between a bag, basket, and tied bundle. The tied-container account explains the early outline more securely than the sun-and-tree interpretation, without fixing every detail of the object.
